concept: Reading bar, pie and line graphs

artifact.topic: Reading bar, pie and line graphs

cards.title: What a bar graph shows
cards.idea: In a bar graph the height of each bar tells you the value for that category, read off against the axis.

interaction.prompt: Tap the tallest bar to find the subject with the most students

cards.reveal: The tallest bar reaches 40 on the axis, so 40 students chose that subject. Taller bar means larger value.

cards.title: Reading a value exactly
cards.idea: To read a bar's value, follow its top across to the scale; if it sits between two marks, estimate.

interaction.prompt: Tap the mark on the scale that matches the top of the highlighted bar

cards.reveal: The bar's top lines up with 25, so its value is 25. Always trace horizontally from the top to the scale.

cards.title: What a pie chart shows
cards.idea: A pie chart splits a whole into slices; a bigger slice means a bigger share of the total.

interaction.prompt: Tap the largest slice to find the most popular fruit

cards.reveal: The largest slice covers half the circle, so that fruit is half of all choices. The full circle is the whole, 100 percent.

cards.title: Slices add to the whole
cards.idea: All the slices of a pie chart together make one full circle, so their percentages add up to 100.

interaction.prompt: Slide to set the missing slice so all slices total 100 percent

cards.reveal: With slices of 30, 25 and 20 percent, the missing slice must be 25 percent, because 30 plus 25 plus 20 plus 25 makes 100.

cards.title: What a line graph shows
cards.idea: A line graph plots values over time; the line rising means increase, falling means decrease.

interaction.prompt: Tap the part of the line where the value is falling

cards.reveal: Between March and April the line slopes down, so the value decreased there. A rising line would mean it grew.

cards.title: Choosing the right graph
cards.idea: Bar graphs compare categories, pie charts show parts of a whole, line graphs show change over time.

interaction.prompt: Tap the graph type best for showing temperature across a week

cards.reveal: A line graph is best, because it shows how a value changes over time, day by day.
